intro: What's up, football fans! Today we've got twenty-five crazy NFL facts that you've probably never heard before. Some are weird, some are wild, and some will totally change the way you watch the game. Stick around until the very end, because the last one is a sticky situation. Let's kick it off!
outro: And that's all twenty-five! Which fact surprised you the most? Tell me in the comments! Check out one of these videos next, and don't forget to subscribe for more crazy facts. See you next time!

facts.title: The first pro player
facts.narration: Fact number one! The very first professional football player was William Pudge Heffelfinger. Back in eighteen ninety-two, the Allegheny Athletic Association secretly paid him five hundred dollars to play in a single game. That was a lot of money back then! Today, that piece of paper is one of the most important documents in football history!

facts.title: Born in a car dealership
facts.narration: Fact number two! The NFL was born in nineteen twenty, inside a car dealership in Canton, Ohio. A group of team owners sat on the running boards of the cars and created a new league. It was first called the American Professional Football Association, and it got the name National Football League two years later!

facts.title: A $100 team
facts.narration: Fact number three! When the league started, the entry fee for a team was just one hundred dollars. Today, NFL teams are worth billions of dollars, and the Dallas Cowboys are one of the most valuable sports teams on the entire planet. Talk about a good investment!

facts.title: Owned by the fans
facts.narration: Fact number four! The Green Bay Packers don't have one rich owner. They are owned by their fans! Hundreds of thousands of people own shares of the team. The shares don't pay any money, and you can't really sell them, but fans buy them anyway, just to say they own a piece of the Packers!

facts.title: Named after a toy
facts.narration: Fact number five! The Super Bowl got its name from a kid's toy. Team owner Lamar Hunt watched his children playing with a bouncy rubber ball called a Super Ball. He jokingly suggested the name Super Bowl for the big game, and even though he thought it was silly, the name stuck forever!

facts.title: Twelve-dollar tickets
facts.narration: Fact number six! Tickets for the very first Super Bowl in nineteen sixty-seven cost about twelve dollars. And get this, the game didn't even sell out! Thousands of seats were empty. Today, a single Super Bowl ticket can cost thousands of dollars!

facts.title: Roman numerals
facts.narration: Fact number seven! The Super Bowl uses Roman numerals, but that didn't start until Super Bowl five. And there's one big exception. In twenty sixteen, the game was called Super Bowl fifty, with regular numbers, because the Roman numeral L just didn't look very good on the logo!

facts.title: A trophy by Tiffany
facts.narration: Fact number eight! The Vince Lombardi Trophy is handmade by Tiffany and Company, the famous jewelry company. It's made of sterling silver, it weighs about seven pounds, and it takes months to make. And unlike some other trophies, a brand new one is made for the winner every single year!

facts.title: Pigskin isn't pig
facts.narration: Fact number nine! People call a football a pigskin, but NFL footballs are actually made from cowhide! Long ago, early balls were made from inflated pig bladders. Today, every single NFL game ball is made by hand at one Wilson factory in the small town of Ada, Ohio!

facts.title: 108 Super Bowl balls
facts.narration: Fact number ten! For the Super Bowl, the factory makes one hundred and eight special footballs, fifty-four for each team. Every ball is printed with the names of both teams before the game. After the big game, many of those balls become super valuable souvenirs!

facts.title: The president saved football
facts.narration: Fact number eleven! Early football was so dangerous that President Teddy Roosevelt pushed to make the game safer. One of the big changes came in nineteen-oh-six, when the forward pass became legal. Before that, throwing the ball forward wasn't allowed at all! Can you imagine football without passing?

facts.title: The perfect season
facts.narration: Fact number twelve! The nineteen seventy-two Miami Dolphins are the only team in NFL history to have a perfect season. They won every single game, seventeen and zero, including the Super Bowl! Every year, when the last unbeaten team finally loses, some of those old Dolphins players celebrate with champagne!

facts.title: More rings than any team
facts.narration: Fact number thirteen! Tom Brady won seven Super Bowls. That's more than any NFL team has ever won! The Patriots and the Steelers have six each. And here's the crazy part: Brady was picked one hundred and ninety-ninth in the draft, after six other quarterbacks!

facts.title: Playing until 48
facts.narration: Fact number fourteen! George Blanda played professional football for twenty-six seasons. He was a quarterback and a kicker, and he didn't retire until he was forty-eight years old! Some of his teammates weren't even born when he started his career!

facts.title: The Ice Bowl
facts.narration: Fact number fifteen! The coldest NFL game ever is called the Ice Bowl. In nineteen sixty-seven, the Packers played the Cowboys in Green Bay at thirteen degrees below zero! The referees' whistles froze to their lips, so they had to shout instead. The Packers won with a last-second touchdown!

facts.title: Thirteen miles of catches
facts.narration: Fact number sixteen! Jerry Rice is the greatest receiver of all time. He caught passes for twenty-two thousand, eight hundred and ninety-five yards in his career. That's about thirteen miles, almost half a marathon, just from catching the football!

facts.title: The rushing king
facts.narration: Fact number seventeen! Emmitt Smith ran for eighteen thousand, three hundred and fifty-five yards, the most in NFL history. That's more than ten miles of running with the ball, while giant players were trying to tackle him on every single play!

facts.title: Two hundred sacks
facts.narration: Fact number eighteen! Bruce Smith holds the record for the most sacks ever, with two hundred! A sack is when a defender tackles the quarterback before he can throw. That means Bruce Smith knocked down quarterbacks two hundred times. Ouch!

facts.title: The invisible yellow line
facts.narration: Fact number nineteen! That yellow first down line you see on TV? It isn't real! Players on the field can't see it at all. It's a computer graphic that was first used on TV in nineteen ninety-eight, and now it's hard to imagine watching football without it!

facts.title: The Immaculate Reception
facts.narration: Fact number twenty! In nineteen seventy-two, Franco Harris made the most famous catch ever. The ball bounced off another player, and just before it hit the ground, Harris scooped it up and ran for a touchdown to win the game! Fans named it the Immaculate Reception.

facts.title: Billions of wings
facts.narration: Fact number twenty-one! Super Bowl Sunday is one of the biggest eating days of the year. Americans eat about one point four five billion chicken wings during Super Bowl weekend. If you lined them all up, they would wrap around the Earth more than once!

facts.title: The biggest TV show
facts.narration: Fact number twenty-two! The Super Bowl is the biggest TV event in America. Recent games have been watched by more than one hundred and twenty million people! That's why companies pay millions of dollars for just thirty seconds of commercial time!

facts.title: No helmet needed
facts.narration: Fact number twenty-three! Believe it or not, NFL players didn't have to wear helmets until nineteen forty-three! Before that, some players chose to play without one. And the first helmets were made of soft leather, with no face mask at all!

facts.title: Four in a row
facts.narration: Fact number twenty-four! The Buffalo Bills went to the Super Bowl four years in a row, from nineteen ninety-one to nineteen ninety-four. That's amazing! But here's the sad part: they lost all four of them. No other team has ever done that!

facts.title: The Gatorade shower
facts.narration: And fact number twenty-five! The famous Gatorade shower started with the New York Giants in the nineteen eighties. Players dumped a big cooler of Gatorade on coach Bill Parcells after a win. The team kept winning, so they kept doing it, and now coaches all over the league get soaked when they win!
